column1: # Each row states a requirement and names the tests that verify it.
# `tests/traceability.rs` parses this file and fails when a row is
# malformed, when a requirement names no test, or when a named test does
# not exist anywhere in the crate — so a requirement cannot silently lose
# its verification, and a renamed test cannot silently orphan a
# Scope: the compliance requirements introduced by the four frameworks
# requirements that are safety- or security-relevant. It is not a
# transcription of every functional requirement in the spec; claiming
# whole-spec traceability we do not have would defeat the purpose.

column2: Every audit row binds its own content, so editing a row is detectable.
Every audit row binds its predecessor, so deleting or reordering rows is detectable.
Chain digests are reproducible after a JSONB round-trip that reorders keys.
Introducing the chain to a populated table does not produce spurious breaks.
Chain verification is bounded so it cannot be used as a CPU denial-of-service.
A verification result states what it does and does not attest to.
Reads are auditable activity, with a closed action vocabulary.
The caller's declared purpose of use is recorded, normalised, and never echoed verbatim.
An outward disclosure is distinguishable from an internal access (§164.528).
An audit row records both the caller's declaration and the standing deployment declarations.
Erasure destroys content while the audit chain still verifies.
Redaction does not let an attacker detach a redacted row's successor.
An erased record degrades cleanly: the tombstone is a valid, data-free payload.
The erasure record states its legal basis, scale, and irreversibility.
Erasure is destructive under ABAC, so a write-tier caller cannot reach it.
A cross-border transfer is never asserted without a declared residency and destination.
EHDS secondary use is separable from primary care delivery.
Every rendered resource declares the profile it claims conformance to.
The claimed profile is family-local, not a false US Core conformance claim.
Resources this service renders conform to the profile it declares.
Missing must-support elements and broken cardinalities are errors.
An identifier without a namespace is rejected, so a bare value cannot become an identity.
A code in a required-bound value set is validated, not merely present.
An unbound code system warns rather than failing, preserving foreign namespaces.
Validation surfaces the service's own payload rules, not only FHIR conformance.
The CapabilityStatement's declared search parameters match the supported set.
SMART discovery is emitted only when a real authorization server is configured.
Discovery documents stay reachable without a credential when enforcement is on.
Bulk export output is well-formed NDJSON, one resource per line.
A truncated export declares itself rather than presenting as a complete population.
The completion manifest carries the Bulk Data IG's required fields.
Export state is durable and bounded: it survives the process, expires, and cancelling releases the output at once.
Export artifacts are confined to the store base: a crafted file:// reference cannot read outside it (SEC-B4).
A safety classification is declared with its rationale, defaulting conservatively.
The SBOM is derived from the real dependency graph and cannot drift from the binary.
Every direct dependency carries a purpose and a safety-relevance note (§8.1.2).
The register cannot retain entries for dependencies that were removed.
The SBOM is valid CycloneDX and carries the lifecycle evidence fields.
SBOM rendering is deterministic, so a reproducible build yields an identical SBOM.
A release is reported as reproducible only with full build provenance.
The posture report states what each framework is NOT claimed to satisfy.
Missing or invalid credentials are 401; a valid credential denied by policy is 403.
Clinical codes are structurally validated against their declared coding system.
Deterministic identifiers are validated, because a shared value short-circuits matching to 1.0.
Every free-text field, array, and array entry is size-capped before storage or matching.
A merge folds the duplicate into the survivor without losing data or duplicating entries.
Under the outbox transport the entity write, its event, and its audit row commit atomically.
